long_biography.plain_text:
Clipper founder Steve Parkin helped open its recruitment to people leaving prison through a partnership with Tempus Novo. At Northampton, a pilot with HMP Spring Hill allowed men to work at the company during the day and return to prison afterwards. The charity planned to continue supporting those who stayed in work after release.

His involvement in racing also extended to bringing others into ownership. For the Bronte Collection syndicate, Parkin supplied horses from his farm or bought them himself, while his friends paid the training bills. If a horse was sold, they shared the proceeds. The arrangement encouraged former owners among his business and personal contacts to return to the sport.
